771	You understand what a gaon he was. I once gave a class in Tel Aviv, in a synagogue where he was the rabbi,
772	a synagogue in Tel Aviv, and the gabbai told me, and I later saw it written in books too,
773	that once Rav Ovadia kept a night watch.
774	He wasn't yet Rishon LeTzion then, so he would sit, and others would sit and learn too, they didn't bother
775	him much.
776	So there was a young man sitting and keeping the night watch as well.
777	He wanted to take a book from the top shelf.
778	Now he couldn't reach the top shelf, so he climbed with his shoes on the bench of the beit midrash, and climbed up to take
779	the book, he came to take the book.
780	The gabbai saw this.
781	What are you doing?
782	In your own house do you also climb on the couches with your shoes like that?
783	He said to him: but how will I reach?
784	He said to him: I don't care how you'll reach, you won't climb up here with shoes on the couches,

792	He took off his jacket.
793	He put the jacket on the upholstery and said to him: now go up and take your book.

795	That's what Chacham Ovadia did, that's it, and he sat and learned.
